target.title: feat(codex): run remote workspaces without splitting app-server
target.body:
Closes #101282

Related: #101221

AI-assisted: yes. I understand the topology, compatibility boundaries, and fail-closed behavior in this change. A sanitized agent transcript was intentionally omitted.

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where operators using remote Codex workspaces had to host Codex app-server separately from Gateway, splitting lifecycle, auth, hooks, thread state, local MCP integration, and filesystem ownership across hosts while relying on upstream's experimental WebSocket transport.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds an explicit experimental remote-execution configuration that keeps Gateway's managed Codex app-server local over stdio and routes only filesystem/process work through an authenticated registry-backed Codex exec-server environment. It requires Codex 0.142+, projects workspace paths, includes the selected environment in runtime identity, rotates unverifiable bindings, prevents `/btw` from forking stale bindings, clears ambient exec-server routing unless this validated surface is enabled, keeps credentials out of durable fingerprints, and fails closed for incompatible sandbox, loopback proxy, Computer Use, and local stdio MCP configurations.

The infrastructure still owns registry availability, executor registration, executor environment sanitization, and equivalent Codex policy/config on the Gateway host. This PR does not make upstream app-server WebSocket transport production-supported. It overlaps the version/startup/lifecycle work in #101221 and must be reconciled with that PR before merge.

## User Impact

Operators can keep one canonical Gateway/app-server control plane while executing inside an independently managed remote workspace. The feature is opt-in under `appServer.experimental.remoteExecution`; explicit local stdio and remote WebSocket configurations remain available, while inherited `CODEX_EXEC_SERVER_*` routing is deliberately ignored unless this validated surface is enabled.

## Evidence

- Focused Codex regression suite: 13 files, 497 tests passed.

  ```text
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/config.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/shared-client.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-startup.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.binding.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.user-mcp-servers.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/plugin-app-cache-key.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-build.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/auth-bridge.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport-stdio.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/side-question.test.ts extensions/codex/src/conversation-binding.test.ts extensions/codex/src/web-search-provider.test.ts
  ```

- Targeted `tsgo` passed for every touched production TypeScript file using a root-extended temporary config.
- Direct `oxlint` passed for every touched TypeScript file.
- `oxfmt --check` passed for all 24 supported touched files; `git diff --check` and plugin manifest JSON parsing passed.
- Mandatory Codex autoreview passed with no accepted/actionable findings.
- Dependency contract checked directly at exact Codex tag `rust-v0.142.5` (`26de83050b20f7e0ee211b9739e52ae00ce8032a`):
  - app-server stdio/WebSocket support status: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.142.5/codex-rs/app-server/README.md#protocol
  - authenticated registry environment construction/default selection: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.142.5/codex-rs/exec-server/src/environment.rs
  - authenticated Noise registry client and reconnect ownership: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.142.5/codex-rs/exec-server/src/remote.rs
- Live registry-backed executor E2E remains pending; no suitable environment registry/executor was available for this checkout. The PR remains draft until that user-path proof exists.
